messages.subject: Shiny for single user UI
parts:
Hi all,
 
I'm going to develop a GUI for an R application that will run on a shared server, and I'm considering the use of shiny for it. The application is intended for single user interaction, so I don't want anyone else than the user that created the page to access it. I understand that this is not exactly what shiny has been built for (what I actually need is a desktop GUI, so probably tcltk would be more appropriate for this task), but I made some tests and shiny behaves quite well for my purposes, and the pages are very easy to code.

So I have three questions:

1 - do you think using shiny for developing desktop-like GUIs is could to lead to problems/limitations?

2 - is there a quick way to make the pages accessible only to the user that spawned them?

3 - is there a way to make runApp select the first available port instead of the default?

Thanks a lot.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Shiny for single user UI
parts:
1) It really depends. If you start to get into a lot of toolbars, buttons, filesystem interaction (besides just uploading/download data), etc. then it will be harder with Shiny unless you know HTML/JavaScript (and even then the filesystem interaction may be extremely difficult to do from the browser). There is very little that is impossible though.

2) Not currently. It will be easier to do this in the future with the paid version of Shiny Server (at least to lock it down to one specific user [or group of users], but that single user could still launch multiple browser windows to the same app and those would be independent sessions).

3) That's not possible at this time, sorry.

messages.subject: Re: Shiny for single user UI
parts:
Hi, thanks for your support.

Point 1 and 3 are not really a problem, since the GUI is not going to be very complex, and I can pass runApp a port number (I will make some system call for getting a free one).

I've been thinking quite a bit about point 2, but the only thing I could come up with is filtering (at least) remote accesses by using the clientData$url_hostname field, as in the Client Data section of the tutorial.This is not intended to be security feature of course, but this way only connections coming form the server box would be served. What about that?

Thanks again
